name: Institutional Decentralization
description: Prescriptive support for dispersing political or administrative authority across smaller, local, federal, or polycentric units.
boundaryStatement: Separate from the descriptive claim that decentralization works well.

poles.negative: Political and administrative authority should not be deliberately dispersed
poles.positive: Political and administrative authority should be dispersed across smaller, local, federal, or polycentric units

name: Institutional Centralization
description: Prescriptive support for concentrating authority in a central institution when uniformity or coordinated capacity is desired.
boundaryStatement: Not simply the inverse of decentralization; institutions can combine central and local competencies.

poles.negative: Political and administrative authority should not be deliberately concentrated
poles.positive: Political and administrative authority should be concentrated centrally when uniform coordination is required

name: Electoral and Institutional Participation
description: Prescriptive use of elections, parties, legislation, litigation, and other formal political channels as means of change.
boundaryStatement: Can coexist with direct action.

poles.negative: Formal electoral and institutional channels should generally be avoided as strategies for change
poles.positive: Elections and formal political institutions are legitimate and useful strategies for political change

name: Direct Action
description: Prescriptive use of strikes, boycotts, occupations, mutual aid, civil resistance, or other action outside ordinary electoral channels.
boundaryStatement: Can coexist with electoral participation; violent tactics are measured separately.

poles.negative: Political change should avoid direct action outside ordinary electoral channels
poles.positive: Direct action outside ordinary electoral channels can be a legitimate and useful strategy for change

name: Revolutionary Rupture
description: Prescriptive support for replacing core institutions through revolutionary rupture rather than only reforming them in place.
boundaryStatement: Does not imply support for violence or a vanguard party.

poles.negative: Core institutions should be changed without revolutionary rupture
poles.positive: Some desired transformations require revolutionary rupture and replacement of core institutions

name: Institutional Reform
description: Prescriptive support for changing existing institutions through constitutional, legislative, administrative, or organizational reform.
boundaryStatement: Can coexist with long-run structural transformation.

poles.negative: Working through reforms of existing institutions is not a legitimate strategy for major change
poles.positive: Existing institutions can be deliberately reformed to achieve major political goals

name: Gradual Transition
description: Prescriptive support for sequencing major change to manage uncertainty, adaptation, and transition costs.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from accepting only minor reforms.

poles.negative: Major changes should not be phased merely to manage transition and uncertainty
poles.positive: Major institutional changes should often be phased to manage uncertainty and transition costs

name: Immediatist Transition
description: Prescriptive support for implementing a desired institutional change rapidly rather than deliberately phasing it.
boundaryStatement: Not synonymous with revolution or violence.

poles.negative: Desired institutional changes should generally be phased rather than implemented rapidly
poles.positive: When an institution is unjust, the desired replacement should sometimes be implemented without deliberate gradualism

name: Income and Wealth Redistribution
description: Prescriptive use of taxes and transfers to alter the distribution of resources after or alongside market incomes.
boundaryStatement: Separate from rules that shape bargaining power and ownership before market income is generated.

poles.negative: Taxes and transfers should not deliberately alter the distribution of market income or wealth
poles.positive: Taxes and transfers should be used when appropriate to reduce unjust material inequality or secure social provision

name: Predistributive Reform
description: Prescriptive alteration of property, bargaining, competition, education, labor, or market rules that shape primary distributions before transfers.
boundaryStatement: Can coexist with redistribution; it is not its opposite.

poles.negative: Policy should not deliberately reshape the rules that generate primary market distributions
poles.positive: Policy should reshape underlying market and bargaining rules when they generate unjust primary distributions

name: Regulatory Intervention
description: Prescriptive use of legal rules and public oversight to constrain market or organizational conduct.
boundaryStatement: Domain-specific; endorsement does not imply maximal regulation in every market.

poles.negative: Public authorities should generally avoid adding regulatory constraints to market conduct
poles.positive: Public regulation and oversight should be used when market or organizational conduct creates serious harms or power imbalances

name: Market Deregulation
description: Prescriptive removal or simplification of regulatory restrictions to expand voluntary market choice and entry.
boundaryStatement: Can coexist with support for some rules protecting rights, competition, or externalities.

poles.negative: Existing market regulations should generally be retained or strengthened rather than deliberately removed
poles.positive: Regulatory restrictions should be removed or simplified when they unnecessarily block voluntary entry, choice, or competition

name: Public Provision
description: Prescriptive use of state or public institutions to directly provide or finance goods and services.
boundaryStatement: Separate from the normative claim that social needs matter and from the design of cash versus in-kind benefits.

poles.negative: Social needs should generally be addressed without direct public provision
poles.positive: Public institutions should directly provide or finance important goods and services when appropriate

name: Exit and Parallel Institutions
description: Prescriptive reliance on voluntary exit, mutual aid, counter-institutions, or parallel provision rather than state monopoly.
boundaryStatement: Does not imply every collective good can be supplied through exit.

poles.negative: Political and social problems should not generally be addressed by building voluntary alternatives outside state provision
poles.positive: Voluntary exit, mutual aid, and parallel institutions should be used to solve problems outside state monopoly when feasible

name: Coercive Political Strategy
description: Prescriptive willingness to use coercive or forceful tactics beyond ordinary rights-protecting enforcement to advance political change.
boundaryStatement: Separate from conditional defensive force and from ordinary enforcement of general law.

poles.negative: Political change should avoid coercive or forceful tactics beyond ordinary rights-protecting enforcement
poles.positive: Coercive or forceful tactics can sometimes be justified to advance political change

name: Nonviolent Strategy
description: Prescriptive commitment to nonviolent methods of political conflict and change.
boundaryStatement: Can include disruptive civil resistance and direct action.

poles.negative: Political strategy need not give nonviolence special priority
poles.positive: Political conflict and social change should be pursued through nonviolent methods

name: Coalitional Compromise
description: Prescriptive willingness to accept partial gains and negotiated compromise with political opponents.
boundaryStatement: A strategy preference, not a substantive ideological midpoint.

poles.negative: Political actors should generally hold out for the full preferred program rather than accept compromise
poles.positive: Political actors should often accept negotiated compromise and partial gains

name: Public Ownership
description: Prescriptive use of public/state/social ownership for productive assets or infrastructure.
boundaryStatement: Does not by itself specify central planning or worker self-management.

poles.negative: Productive assets should not generally be placed in public or social ownership
poles.positive: Public or social ownership should be used for some important productive assets or infrastructure

name: Worker Control
description: Prescriptive use of worker governance, cooperatives, codetermination, or democratic control in productive organizations.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from union bargaining over terms and from state ownership.

poles.negative: Workplace governance should generally remain with owners and appointed managers
poles.positive: Workers should exercise substantial governance or democratic control in productive organizations

name: Social Insurance
description: Prescriptive use of broad social insurance, income security, pensions, health insurance, or related risk-pooling institutions.
boundaryStatement: Does not determine contributory versus universal design.

poles.negative: Social risks should generally be handled without broad collective insurance institutions
poles.positive: Broad social-insurance institutions should pool major social risks and protect people against predictable vulnerability

name: Vanguard Party
description: Prescriptive support for a disciplined revolutionary party claiming a leading role in political transition.
boundaryStatement: A direct Marxist-Leninist discriminator, not a generic measure of organization or leadership.

poles.negative: Political transition should not be led by a disciplined revolutionary vanguard party
poles.positive: A disciplined revolutionary vanguard party should lead the transition to socialism or communism

name: Democratic Centralism
description: Prescriptive support for internal deliberation followed by binding organizational unity in a Leninist party structure.
boundaryStatement: Specific to Leninist organizational doctrine; not equivalent to ordinary party discipline.

poles.negative: Political organizations should not require binding centralized unity after internal deliberation
poles.positive: A revolutionary party should combine internal deliberation with binding centralized unity after decisions

name: Constitutional Reform
description: Prescriptive use of constitutional rules, rights, courts, checks, and formal institutional design to constrain political power.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from generic reform and from the descriptive quality of courts or experts.

poles.negative: Constitutional rules and formal checks should not be a major instrument for constraining political power
poles.positive: Constitutional rules, rights, checks, and institutional design should be used to constrain political power

name: Subsidiarity
description: Prescriptive allocation of public responsibilities to the lowest competent social or political level while permitting higher-level action where required.
boundaryStatement: Not equivalent to unconditional decentralization; higher levels retain roles when lower levels cannot perform the task.

poles.negative: Public responsibilities need not be allocated to lower competent institutions before higher levels act
poles.positive: Public responsibilities should normally rest with the lowest competent social or political level

name: Contestable Institutions
description: Prescriptive design of institutions so exercises of power can be challenged, reviewed, and controlled by affected people.
boundaryStatement: Targets non-domination through institutional design rather than merely distributing authority geographically.

poles.negative: Exercises of public or private power need not be institutionally contestable by affected people
poles.positive: Institutions should provide effective mechanisms for people to contest and review exercises of power

name: Collective Bargaining
description: Prescriptive support for worker organization and collective bargaining as institutions governing employment relations.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from worker ownership or full workplace self-government.

poles.negative: Employment terms should generally be set without collective worker bargaining institutions
poles.positive: Workers should be able to organize and bargain collectively over employment relations

name: Ecological Restructuring
description: Prescriptive restructuring of economic and political institutions to satisfy ecological constraints and sustainability duties.
boundaryStatement: Does not predetermine degrowth, market instruments, public ownership, or one energy technology.

poles.negative: Environmental harms should be addressed without substantial restructuring of economic or political institutions
poles.positive: Economic and political institutions should be restructured where necessary to satisfy ecological constraints and sustainability duties

name: Central Economic Planning
description: Prescriptive allocation of major productive resources through centralized administrative planning rather than primarily decentralized market exchange.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from public ownership: publicly owned firms can use markets and privately owned firms can be heavily directed.

poles.negative: Major productive resources should not be allocated through centralized administrative planning
poles.positive: Major productive resources should be allocated substantially through centralized administrative planning
